svg.title: The four scopes, and where the trust boundary sits in each
svg.desc: Four nested scopes, each one step wider than the last. Solo: you write and your own gate signs, so the boundary is around one person. Team: a shared gate signs for a group, and the reviewer is never the author. Organization: a second gate reviews what a team gate already signed, on its own authority. Commons: the publishing organization signs, then the commons gate countersigns on its own authority before anyone outside can install it. The mechanism is identical at every scope — only the audience and the signing authority widen. Solo is free and stays free; the commons is free to read and free to contribute.
svg.text: FOUR SCOPES — ONE MECHANISM, A WIDER AUDIENCE EACH TIME

g.text: Solo
you, on your own machine
FREE — AND STAYS FREE
Your own gate holds, scans, grades and signs.
The boundary sits around one person: nothing leaves,
and nothing arrives that you did not write.
Team
a group sharing one gate
THE SHARED GATE
One gate signs for the whole group, and the reviewer is
never the author — so a teammate's correction reaches you
already vouched for, by someone who was not them.
Organization
many teams, one authority
A SECOND, INDEPENDENT GATE
A second gate reviews what a team gate already signed, on its
own authority — it can refuse what a team accepted. This is the
step that makes one signature two, and the record exportable.
Commons
anyone, outside your company
FREE TO READ, FREE TO CONTRIBUTE
Your organization signs what it is willing to stand behind; the
commons gate then reviews it again on its own authority. Every
verdict is published — including the refusals.

svg.text: SAME WRITE PATH AT EVERY SCOPE — ONLY THE SIGNING AUTHORITY CHANGES
